subject: cs-9
description: Web fundamentals, HTML structure, tags, hyperlinks, lists, tables, JavaScript syntax, variables, operators, and control structures.

questions.question: A set of related webpages linked together is called a:
questions.explanation: A Website is a collection of related webpages accessible via the internet. A single webpage is one document within that website.

questions.question: What does URL stand for?
questions.explanation: URL stands for Universal Resource Locator — it is the unique address used to access a webpage on the internet.

questions.question: A website where content changes based on user interaction is called:
questions.explanation: A Dynamic website changes its content based on user input or actions. A Static website has fixed content that does not change unless manually updated.

questions.question: Which of the following is used to develop the FRONT-END of a website?
questions.explanation: Front-end development uses HTML (structure), CSS (styling), and JavaScript (interactivity) to create what users see in the browser.

questions.question: What is the Document Object Model (DOM)?

options.B: A tree-like representation of an HTML page used by browsers

questions.explanation: The DOM is a tree structure created by the browser from HTML elements, allowing JavaScript to dynamically access and modify page content.

questions.question: Which HTML tag pair contains the TITLE of a webpage shown in the browser tab?
questions.explanation: The <title> tag pair defines the name shown in the browser tab. The <h1> tag creates a heading visible on the page itself.

questions.question: HTML comments are written using:
questions.explanation: HTML uses <!-- --> for comments. These are not displayed in the browser but help developers annotate their code.

questions.question: Which HTML tag is used to insert a line break?
questions.explanation:
The
tag inserts a line break in HTML. It is a self-closing tag (no ending tag needed).

questions.question: The largest heading in HTML is:
questions.explanation: HTML supports 6 heading levels. <h1> is the largest and most important, while <h6> is the smallest.

questions.question: Back-end development requires:

options.B: Knowledge of server-side languages like PHP, JavaScript (Node.js)

questions.explanation: Back-end development handles server logic and database management using languages like PHP, Node.js, Python — more technical than front-end. ★ Additional Questions — Topics 3.1 to 3.2

questions.question: A single document accessible through the internet is called a:
questions.explanation: A webpage is a single document accessible through the internet. A website is a collection of such related webpages linked together.

questions.question: Which service helps users find websites when they do not know the exact URL?
questions.explanation: A search engine lets users find websites by entering keywords. It searches and displays matching website addresses and brief content summaries.

questions.question: Every website must be uploaded to a __________ so visitors can access it at any time.
questions.explanation: Web hosting services provide web servers that are available round the clock, allowing clients and visitors to access the website on their devices.

questions.question: The first page that appears when a website is opened is called the:
questions.explanation: Every website has a homepage — the first page that loads when a visitor accesses the website's URL, from where they can navigate further.

questions.question: HTML stands for:
questions.explanation: HTML stands for Hypertext Markup Language. It is the primary language used to define and display content in the form of a webpage.

questions.question: In the DOM tree, which node sits at the very TOP as the root?
questions.explanation: In the DOM tree, 'Document' is the root node at the top. Below it comes the <html> node, which then branches into <head> and <body>.

questions.question: The standard file extension for an HTML document is:
questions.explanation: HTML files are saved with the.html extension. this is the standard extension for HTML documents.

questions.question: Which IDE is specifically mentioned in the FBISE Class 9 textbook for Chapter 3 activities?
questions.explanation: specifically states that Visual Studio 2022 is used for this chapter, noting that codes apply to any other environment as well.

questions.question: A web application differs from a website because it:

options.B: Executes tasks and provides services via a browser and internet
options.D: Cannot be accessed from a mobile device

questions.explanation: A web application remotely accesses a server to execute tasks (like a CRM system), unlike a website which only shares information.

questions.question: In the DOM tree, the <body> node holds:

options.B: The main visible content like headings and paragraphs

questions.explanation: The body node is where content of HTML is placed — headings, paragraphs, unordered lists, etc..

questions.question: HTML is described in as a:
questions.explanation: HTML is a 'tag based programming language' where characters between angle brackets define and display content.

questions.question: Which part of a website is referred to as the Graphical User Interface (GUI)?
questions.explanation: the front-end as providing the GUI — the graphical interface that visitors view and interact with in their browser.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT mentioned in as a scripting language for dynamic websites?
questions.explanation: JavaScript, Python, PHP, and ASP.Net for dynamic websites. Assembly language is low-level system code, not used for web scripting.

questions.question: In HTML, the <html> tag-pair:

options.B: Wraps and identifies the entire HTML document
options.C: Defines the visible body content only

questions.explanation: Anything written between the <html> tag-pair is recognized as an HTML document..

questions.question: Once a static webpage loads on a user's device, the connection to the web server is:
questions.explanation: After a static website loads on the client's computer, the link to the server is no longer required — it runs independently.. Topic 3.2.3 to 3.3 — HTML Tags, Images, Tables, Links & CSS

questions.question: Which HTML attribute specifies the path to an image file?
questions.explanation: The src (source) attribute specifies where the image file is located. The alt attribute provides alternative text if the image fails to load.

questions.question: Which tag pair defines a ROW in an HTML table?
questions.explanation: The <tr> (table row) tag defines a row in a table. <td> defines a data cell and <th> defines a header cell within that row.

questions.question: Which CSS type has the HIGHEST priority when all three types are present?
questions.explanation: Priority order: Inline > Embedded > External. Inline CSS applied directly to an element always overrides other types.

questions.question: To open a hyperlink in a new browser tab, which target value is used?
questions.explanation: _blank opens the link in a new tab/window. _self (default) opens it in the same tab.

questions.question: CSS stands for:
questions.explanation: CSS (Cascading Style Sheets) is a stylesheet language used to control the presentation, layout, and design of HTML documents.

questions.question: Embedded CSS is placed:
questions.explanation: Embedded CSS uses a <style> tag pair in the <head> section. External CSS is in a separate file, while Inline CSS is on each element.

questions.question: What does the <strong> tag do in HTML?

options.B: Makes text bold and semantically important

questions.explanation: <strong> makes text bold AND signals semantic importance. <b> makes text bold visually only. <em> adds italic emphasis.

questions.question: Which HTML tag is used to add a video to a webpage?
questions.explanation: The <video> tag is used to embed video content in HTML. The controls attribute adds play/pause/volume controls.

questions.question: The 'href' attribute in a hyperlink specifies:

options.A: The color of the link text
options.C: The size of the linked page
options.D: Whether to open in a new tab

questions.explanation: href (Hypertext Reference) specifies the URL that the hyperlink points to. target specifies how it opens.

questions.question: What is the advantage of External CSS over Inline CSS for a large website?

options.B: Changes in one file apply to all linked pages
options.D: It can only be used with JavaScript

questions.explanation: External CSS allows site-wide style changes in one.css file rather than modifying every element individually — essential for large projects. ★ Additional Questions — Topics 3.2.3 to 3.3

questions.question: Which HTML tag-pair defines a TABLE HEADER cell?
questions.explanation: The <th> tag defines a header cell in a table. It is typically bold and centered by default, used in the first row for column labels.

questions.question: Which HTML tag-pair defines a DATA cell inside a table row?
questions.explanation: The <td> (table data) tag defines individual data cells inside a table row. <td> used on lines 14-16 and 19-21 in its table example.

questions.question: The 'alt' attribute in the tag is used to:

options.C: Provide alternative text if the image fails to load
options.D: Link the image to a URL

questions.explanation: The alt parameter 'provides description of the image' — it shows if the image cannot load and aids accessibility..

questions.question: Hyperlinks in HTML are created using which tag?
questions.explanation: Hyperlinks in HTML use the <a> (anchor) tag-pair. The href attribute inside it specifies the destination URL or path.

questions.question: Which parameter in the <video> tag enables on-screen play, pause, and volume controls?
questions.explanation: The 'controls' parameter in the <video> tag enables the on-screen play/pause and volume controls for the user,.

questions.question: The 'autoplay' parameter in a <video> tag causes the video to:

options.B: Automatically play when the webpage loads

questions.explanation: Autoplay automatically starts the video when the webpage loads but does not provide play/pause or volume controls unless specified separately.

questions.question: What file extension is used for an External CSS file?
questions.explanation: External CSS is saved in a separate file with the.css extension, then linked to HTML via a <link> tag in the <head> section.

questions.question: Inline CSS is written:

options.C: Directly inside an HTML element using the style attribute

questions.explanation: Inline CSS is applied directly on an HTML element. Example: <h1 style='color:red;'>. It has the highest priority of all three CSS types.

questions.question: If both Embedded CSS and External CSS are applied to the same element, which one takes priority?
questions.explanation: priority order: Inline > Embedded > External. Embedded CSS overrides External CSS for the same element.

questions.question: To adjust the display size of an image differently from its actual file size, which attributes are used?
questions.explanation: the dimensions of the image can also be mentioned in terms of width and height, otherwise it will load the image in its actual size..

questions.question: The <table> tag-pair in HTML is used to:
questions.explanation: The <table> tag-pair wraps the entire table. Inside it, <tr> defines rows, <th> defines header cells, and <td> defines data cells.

questions.question: When 'muted' is combined with 'autoplay' in a <video> tag, the video:

options.C: Plays automatically but with sound turned off

questions.explanation: When 'muted' is used, 'the clip loads but volume is muted and needs to be unmuted manually'..

questions.question: External CSS is described in as best suited for:
questions.explanation: External CSS are used with large projects, like in commercial purposes. — one file manages styles for all linked pages.

questions.question: Hyperlinks in HTML can be associated with:
questions.explanation: Hyperlinks can be associated not only to text, but to images as well. This is done using the <a> tag wrapping the element.

questions.question: Which HTML tag-pair is used to define the entire table in 's table example?
questions.explanation: the table starting with the <table> tag-pair. <tr> defines rows inside it, and <th> or <td> define cells within each row. Topic 3.4 to 3.6 — JavaScript, Loops, Functions & Debugging

questions.question: JavaScript is primarily used for:

options.B: Making web pages dynamic and interactive

questions.explanation: JavaScript is a client-side scripting language used to add interactivity, handle events, and create dynamic content on web pages.

questions.question: Which JavaScript data type stores true or false values?
questions.explanation: Boolean variables store only true or false values. Strings store text, Numbers store numeric values.

questions.question: In JavaScript, 'score' and 'Score' are:

options.A: The same variable because JS ignores case
options.B: Two different variables because JS is case-sensitive
options.D: Identical because numeric prefixes are not allowed

questions.explanation: JavaScript is case-sensitive. 'score' and 'Score' are treated as completely different variables by the JavaScript engine.

questions.question: Which operator gives the REMAINDER of a division in JavaScript?
questions.explanation: The modulus operator (%) returns the remainder of division. Example: 10 % 3 = 1.

questions.question: The 'alert()' function in JavaScript:

options.B: Displays a pop-up message box to the user

questions.explanation: alert() displays a dialog box with a message and an OK button — commonly used to notify users of events or results.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly defines a 'for loop' in JavaScript?
questions.explanation: A for loop has three parts: initialization (starting value), condition (when to stop), and update (how to increment/change index).

questions.question: In a nested loop, the inner loop:

options.B: Runs completely for each iteration of the outer loop
options.C: Runs after the outer loop finishes
options.D: Runs simultaneously with the outer loop

questions.explanation: In nested loops, every time the outer loop completes one iteration, the inner loop runs through ALL its iterations from start to finish.

questions.question: Which variable type in JavaScript can be accessed from anywhere in the program?
questions.explanation: Global variables are declared outside functions and can be accessed anywhere. Local variables exist only within the function they are declared in.

questions.question: What is debugging in programming?

options.A: Writing the first version of a program
options.C: Locating and fixing errors in code

questions.explanation: Debugging is the systematic process of finding and fixing bugs (errors) in a program's code.

questions.question: A 'breakpoint' in debugging allows a programmer to:

options.B: Pause program execution at a specific line to inspect variable values
options.C: Skip to the end of the program

questions.explanation: Breakpoints pause execution at marked lines, letting developers inspect the program state and variable values at that exact moment. ★ Additional Questions — Topics 3.4 to 3.6

questions.question: In JavaScript, a variable is declared using which keyword?
questions.explanation: A variable in JavaScript is declared with the 'var' keyword.. Multiple variables can also be declared in the same line.

questions.question: Which of the following is a VALID JavaScript variable name?
questions.explanation: JavaScript variable names cannot start with a number, contain spaces, or use reserved words. _totalMarks follows all naming rules correctly.

questions.question: The first ever assignment of a value to a variable is called:
questions.explanation: initialization as 'the first ever assignment of a value to a variable in the life span of a program'.

questions.question: An array in JavaScript is best described as:

options.A: A single variable that stores only one value
options.B: A loop that runs a fixed number of times
options.C: A data type that holds multiple homogenous elements
options.D: A function that returns true or false

questions.explanation: an array as 'a datatype which can hold a number of homogenous set of elements', avoiding the need for many separate variables.

questions.question: Array indexing in JavaScript starts at:
questions.explanation: it is trivial to note that array-index starts with 0.. So the first element of an array is accessed at index 0.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of a function in JavaScript?

options.C: To group reusable lines of code that can be called repeatedly
options.D: To connect the webpage to a database

questions.explanation: a function as 'a set of lines which occurs in the code quite often that can be segmented once, and called again and again'.

questions.question: Variables declared INSIDE a function in JavaScript are:

options.A: Global and accessible anywhere in the program
options.B: Local and limited to that function only
options.C: Permanent for the entire program run

questions.explanation: Function arguments are 'variables local to that function and their life span is limited to the said function'..

questions.question: The JavaScript 'if-else' statement is used for:

options.C: Making decisions based on a condition

questions.explanation: The if-else (conditional/selection) statement executes a block if a condition is true, and another block if the condition is false.

questions.question: In a 'for loop', the UPDATE part (third section) controls:

options.A: The starting value of the index
options.B: The condition at which the loop stops
options.C: How the index value changes after each iteration
options.D: The output of the loop body

questions.explanation: the step-size defines 'how many steps the index will take after each iteration, till the terminating condition is met'.

questions.question: Which JavaScript comparison operator checks if two values are NOT equal?
questions.explanation: The != operator means 'is not equal to'. 's Table 3-4 lists it as one of the comparison operators used in conditional statements.

questions.question: In Visual Studio.Net, a breakpoint is displayed as:

options.A: A yellow arrow at the line
options.B: A green dot at the start of the line
options.C: A blue star next to the line
options.D: A red dot at the start of the line

questions.explanation: In Visual Studio.Net, a breakpoint is shown as a red dot at the start of line., as illustrated in Fig-41.

questions.question: The 'Step Into' debugging option allows a programmer to:

options.A: Skip directly to the last line
options.B: Run the full program without pausing
options.C: Trace code execution line by line

questions.explanation: 'Step Into' as going through 'the code line by line, as the program will normally execute, so that you have a thorough tracing capability'.

questions.question: JavaScript code is embedded inside an HTML file using:
questions.explanation: JavaScript code is embedded in HTML using the <script> tag-pair. it used in the body with type='text/javascript'.

questions.question: JavaScript 'does not consume much memory' because it is used:.

options.B: At the client-end for making pages dynamic

questions.explanation: JavaScript is used 'at the client-end in developing websites, for making pages dynamic' — running in the browser, not on the server.

questions.question: Which of the following built-in JavaScript functions is explicitly mentioned in ?
questions.explanation: prompt() and input() as examples of built-in JavaScript functions that programmers can call without writing their own code.
